title: Validation of PECARN as a clinical decision rule for CT imaging of children with blunt abdominal trauma: a single centre retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Blunt traumatic injuries are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children. Contrast enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the best imaging tool for screening patients at risk of blunt abdominal injury. Concerns existed on potential overuse and the radiation risks. We aim at evaluating paediatric use of trauma CT scan. Methods Children with traumatic injuries who attended a tertiary trauma centre from January 2000 to December 2024 were included to evaluate the use of trauma CT scan and patterns of paediatric abdominal trauma. We excluded those with penetrating or isolated head injury. The Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network (PECARN) algorithm was applied retrospectively with the aim of validating the use of PECARN. Results Total of 1138 paediatic trauma admissions were identified during the study period and 70% (n 802) had blunt trauma. 483 patients were included after excluding patients with isolated head injury and missing data. 90 days trauma related mortality was 0.7% with one patient died within 24 hours of admission. Overall Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 3.52±5.95 which appeared to increase with age (rho 0.289, p <0.01).111 patients received CT scan, among which 35 are whole body CT. Significant findings were detected in 30% of these scans, 25 required intervention. Patients with higher trauma index and lower GCS, trauma call activation, older aged at presentation were more likely to receive a scan (p<0.001). No pathology was missed in the no CT group. PECARN validation was performed on 200 patients, There were no missed scans and pathologies in PECARN negative patients. Sensitivity was 100%, specificity was 96.5%, negative predictive value was 100%. Conclusion A significant portion of children had negative trauma CT scan and did not need intervention. Use of clinical decision rule is warranted in identifying children at lower risk to minimize unnecessary imaging.

title: Routine pulmonary wound closure after thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations in children: impact on early recovery, one-year CT-based lung expansion, and the learning curve.
abstract: Background The necessity of routine pulmonary parenchymal wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for congenital lung malformations (CLMs) in children remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association of routine wound closure with drainage-related recovery, perioperative outcomes, one-year computed tomography (CT)-based lung re-expansion, and the procedural learning curve. Methods Consecutive children who underwent thoracoscopic sublobar resection for CLMs between January 2021 and March 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. The cohort was divided into a non-closure group and a routine-closure group according to wound management strategy. Pulmonary wound closure was performed using an absorbable barbed suture, generally proceeding from the peripheral or lower-tension side toward the central or higher-tension region. Irregular wounds were managed by initiating closure from multiple peripheral points converging centrally while preserving the natural axis of residual bronchi and vasculature. Outcomes included chest tube duration, drainage volume, prolonged air leak, chest tube reinsertion, postoperative hospital stay, perioperative complications, one-year CT-based volumetric indices, and closure-time learning curve metrics. Results A total of 285 children were included, comprising 75 in the non-closure group and 210 in the closure group. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-closure group, the closure group exhibited significantly shorter chest tube duration (0.87 ± 0.74 vs. 2.81 ± 1.99 days, P < 0.001), lower postoperative drainage volume (2.12 ± 0.70 vs. 7.21 ± 2.58 mL/kg/day, P < 0.001), reduced rates of prolonged air leak and drainage failure, and shorter postoperative hospital stay (5.63 ± 0.83 vs. 7.68 ± 2.10 days, P < 0.001). At one-year follow-up, CT-based volumetric assessment revealed no evidence that wound closure restricted residual lung re-expansion. Closure time decreased from approximately 22 min in the early phase to 11 min in the late phase, with learning curve inflection points identified at cases 47 and 135. Conclusions Routine pulmonary wound closure following thoracoscopic sublobar resection for pediatric CLMs was associated with improved drainage-related recovery and shorter hospitalization, without compromising one-year lung re-expansion on CT. Although closure adds a procedural step, efficiency improved substantially with experience, demonstrating a quantifiable learning curve.

title: Effectiveness of prenatal predictors for congenital diaphragmatic hernia on survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation requirement: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Introduction Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC). Methods CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated. Results 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge. Conclusion O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

title: Relative frequency of non-Wilms renal tumours in children: an institutional experience from a national tertiary referral centre in Malaysia.
abstract: Purpose International protocols for paediatric renal tumours are largely based on Western data with Wilms tumour (WT) accounting for more than 90% of cases. We aimed to evaluate the relative frequency of WT and Non-Wilms Renal Tumours (NWRTs) in a diverse Asian cohort in Malaysia. Methods A retrospective review was conducted of all primary paediatric renal tumours treated at a national tertiary referral centre from 2015 to 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed via post-operative histopathology. Results Of 95 children (median age 29 months), all were Asian descent (73.7% Malay, 9.5% Chinese, 6.3% Indian). WT accounted for only 68.4% of cases, while NWRTs accounted for 31.6%. Among NWRTs, 63.3% were malignant, primarily clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK, n = 7) and renal cell carcinoma (RCC, n = 4). In the classic WT age range (6-84 months), WT prevalence was only 75.6%, with CCSK representing 9.0%. Congenital mesoblastic nephroma (CMN) predominated in infants < 6 months (71.4%), while RCC was exclusively seen in children > 84 months (40.0%). Conclusion The substantial proportion of malignant NWRTs observed in this institutional cohort highlights potential risks of neoadjuvant chemotherapy without histological confirmation. Histopathological diagnosis via percutaneous core-needle biopsy or primary surgery may be highly considered in similar clinical settings.

title: [The eye as a mirror of the heart-retinal findings in heart failure and cardiovascular diseases].
abstract: Background Due to its unique anatomical and functional characteristics, the retina represents a promising organ for the evaluation of systemic vascular diseases. Modern imaging techniques, particularly optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A), enable noninvasive and quantitative assessment of retinal microcirculation. The aim of this review is to present current findings on the significance of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases, with a focus on heart failure. Results Numerous studies show associations between retinal vascular changes and arterial hypertension, coronary heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure. Changes in retinal vascular parameters such as vascular density and perfusion density correlate with structural and functional cardiac changes. Patients with retinal vascular occlusions have an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and higher cardiovascular mortality. Initial studies in patients with acute decompensated heart failure have demonstrated changes in retinal vascular and perfusion density that can be reversed by recompensation. These observations led to the introduction of the term "cardio-ocular syndrome," which describes the interactions between cardiac function, systemic congestion, and retinal microcirculation. Conclusion Retinal imaging opens up new possibilities for the noninvasive assessment of systemic microcirculatory disorders in cardiovascular diseases. OCT‑A could contribute in the future to risk stratification, assessment of disease progression, and monitoring of therapy in heart failure.

title: Peripheral vessel tortuosity index and prognosis in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: Background and aims The peripheral vessel tortuosity index (TI) was proposed to discriminate procedural success in patients undergoing transcatheter endovascular aortic replacement but not in those undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We aimed to investigate the TI and its prognostic relevance in patients undergoing transfemoral (Tf) TAVI. Methods Retrospective, observational single-center study, including patients undergoing Tf-TAVI from April 2011 to January 2023 at the TUM University Hospital, German Heart Centre, and available computed tomography angiography (CTA). Peripheral vessel measurements were performed using dedicated software (3mensio, Pie Medical). TI was determined dividing true central lumen vessel length from centerline reconstruction and direct distance from the aorto-iliac bifurcation to the epigastric artery. TI was dichotomized based on severity according to EVAR guidelines, where a TI of 1.5 is considered discriminatory for nonsevere tortuosity [< 1.5 for low TI (LTI)] and > 1.5 for high TI (HTI)]. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 definitions were applied to describe procedural and follow-up outcomes. Mortality at 6-month follow-up was evaluated. Results We included 2002 patients. Overall age was 81 years [77, 85], 45.2% were female, EuroScore II was 4.22 [2.39, 7.60]. Age (p < 0.001), female sex (p < 0.001), diabetes (p < 0.001), peripheral artery disease (p = 0.002), myocardial infarction (p = 0.013), and creatinine (p = 0.001) were associated with tortuosity. Adjusted 6-month analysis showed that TI > 1.50 was associated with increased mortality [hazard ratio (HR) 1.679, 95% CI (1.098-2.567), p = 0.017]. Conclusions TI > 1.50 may determine a higher-risk population in patients undergoing Tf-TAVI. Further study is required to validate our findings.

title: [Cardiac involvement in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies].
abstract: Background Cardiac manifestations in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) occur more frequently than they are clinically recognized and are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. In particular, subclinical myocarditis often remains undetected due to nonspecific or absent symptoms. Objective This review aims to summarize the prevalence, pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, diagnostic strategies and therapeutic options of cardiac involvement in IIM and to provide practical recommendations for rheumatologists. Methods A scoping review on cardiac manifestations in IIM was performed. A structured literature search was conducted using the PubMed database. The search strategy included combinations of relevant keywords and MeSH terms. Primarily, English language original studies, systematic reviews and current guideline publications related to cardiac involvement in IIM were considered. Studies were selected based on clinical relevance, methodological quality and recency. Results The reported prevalence of cardiac involvement in IIM ranges from 4-26%, depending on the subtype and diagnostic approach. In addition to clinically overt myocarditis, subclinical abnormalities are common and can be detected in up to 50% of patients using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI). Pathophysiological mechanisms include immune-mediated myocardial injury, microvascular dysfunction and fibrotic remodelling. The initial diagnostic work-up should comprise taking a medical history, electrocardiography, measurement of cardiac biomarkers and echocardiography. The use of CMRI represents the diagnostic gold standard and enables sensitive detection of inflammatory and fibrotic myocardial changes. Therapeutically, early initiation of drug treatment, typically high-dose glucocorticoids combined with additional immunomodulating agents, constitutes the cornerstone of management. Conclusion Cardiac manifestations in IIM are common, prognostically relevant and frequently underestimated in clinical practice. A structured diagnostic approach with early use of CMRI and interdisciplinary management is essential to detect subclinical disease and guide appropriate treatment.

title: Notch-referenced mediolateral verification of tibial tunnel position in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: a 3D imaging validation study.
abstract: Background Non-anatomic tibial tunnel placement remains a leading contributor to anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) failure. Mediolateral (ML) tunnel positioning is particularly difficult intraoperatively because no consistent bony landmark defines the lateral footprint border. Purpose To evaluate the accuracy of a novel intraoperative Notch-Referenced Mediolateral (NRML) verification technique by comparing the ML position of the tibial tunnel center (TTC) on postoperative 3D CT with the native tibial footprint center (TFC) on preoperative 3D MRI. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 108 consecutive patients underwent primary all-inside single-bundle ACLR with intraoperative NRML verification. This arthroscopic technique uses the intercondylar notch as a visual reference to verify mediolateral tibial tunnel position before definitive drilling. Conclusion In this single-arm cohort,NRML verification is a simple, equipment-free technique that placed the tibial tunnel within ~1 mm of the native ML footprint, with high measurement reliability. title: First-in-human prospective pilot study of a bipolar dual-center total wrist arthroplasty: early mechanical stability and clinical outcomes.
abstract: Purpose Total wrist arthroplasty (TWA) is limited by implant loosening, instability, and non-physiological load transfer, partly because most contemporary implants rely on a single center of rotation and do not preserve native wrist kinematics. This first-in-human pilot study evaluated the feasibility, early mechanical stability, and clinical outcomes of a novel bipolar dual-center TWA system designed to preserve radiocarpal and midcarpal motion. Methods This prospective single-center pilot case series included five consecutive patients with end-stage wrist arthritis treated with a bipolar dual-center TWA implant using cement fixation, as per the device's intended use. The outcome measures included pain assessed using the pain subscale of the Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE) questionnaire (normalized to a 0-10 scale), total PRWE score, DASH score, range of motion, grip strength, radiographic implant stability, complications, and reoperation. Clinical outcomes were assessed at the most recent follow-up visit. Results The mean follow-up was 19.2 months (range, 12-24 months), with 24-month data available for three patients. Implant survivorship was 100%, with no loosening, migration, dislocation, or implant revision observed on radiographs. One patient experienced a traumatic postoperative fall without loss of implant fixation. The mean PRWE-derived pain score improved from 9.0 to 3.0, and the mean PRWE total improved from 84.6 to 23.2 at the final follow-up. The mean DASH score improved from 79.0 to 29.5, with substantial inter-patient variability (final range, 0-91.7). All five patients met the predefined responder criterion of ΔPRWE ≥ 20 combined with radiographic stability. Three patients with positive preoperative signs of carpal tunnel syndrome subsequently underwent carpal tunnel release 4-8 months postoperatively, with symptomatic improvement in all patients. One intraoperative carpal fracture was managed without component revision surgery. The mean wrist flexion improved from 13° to 37°, and extension improved from 11° to 32°. Conclusions This first-in-human pilot study demonstrated the technical feasibility and early mechanical stability of the bipolar dual-center TWA concept. All patients met the predefined wrist-specific responder criteria with stable mechanical implant fixation. These findings support further investigation of the dual-center concept in larger studies with longer follow-up periods.

title: The boundary between microbial detection and implant-related infection: a structured narrative review of analytical credibility, biological persistence, host response, and clinical causality.
abstract: Background Unexpected microbial signals are frequently encountered in patients with orthopaedic implants who do not satisfy validated criteria for confirmed infection. The central interpretive problem is not limited to periprosthetic joint infection (PJI); it also arises in fracture-fixation and spinal instrumentation, and it involves conventional culture, sonication, histopathology, broad-range polymerase chain reaction (PCR), 16 S rRNA sequencing, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Methods We performed a structured narrative review of literature identified in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science, updated through 27 June 2026. Eligible publications addressed microbial or biofilm-associated signals in orthopaedic implants without unequivocal infection at the time of sampling, or reported outcomes after unexpected positive cultures. Evidence was organized by implant type, indication for implant removal, detection method, host-response evidence, and longitudinal outcome. Particular attention was paid to the distinction between routinely removed fracture-fixation devices and failure-related arthroplasty or spinal revisions. Results Routine removal of fracture-fixation devices provides the least confounded clinical window and demonstrates that microbial signals may be recovered from implants in the absence of recognized failure or overt infection. By contrast, arthroplasty and spinal cohorts labelled "presumed aseptic" are intrinsically confounded because pain, loosening, osteolysis, or pseudarthrosis may represent occult infection. Molecular positivity is further limited by low-biomass contamination and inability to distinguish viable organisms from relic DNA. Favorable outcomes after revision do not prove that infection was never present, because revision surgery itself may eradicate or substantially reduce an occult microbial burden. Conclusions Microbial detection should be interpreted through three sequential domains: analytical credibility, biological activity or persistence, and clinical causality supported by host response or implant-related pathology. "Stable coexistence" is best treated as a longitudinal clinical phenotype or testable mechanistic hypothesis, not as an established diagnostic category. This framework complements, but does not replace, validated PJI, fracture-related infection (FRI), or other implant-specific definitions.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of standard practice wrist MRI for scapholunate ligament injuries: a retrospective arthroscopic correlation study.
abstract: Introduction The scapholunate ligament is the most injured intercarpal ligament. Untreated tears can lead to carpal instability and subsequent radiocarpal and midcarpal osteoarthritis. While wrist arthroscopy remains the gold standard, the diagnostic performance of standard practice preoperative MRI in clinical practice warrants further investigation. Methods We retrospectively analysed patients who underwent preoperative wrist MRI followed by wrist arthroscopy between 2013 and 2021. MRI findings regarding scapholunate ligament integrity were compared with arthroscopic findings serving as reference standard. Sensitivity and specificity were calculated for detection of any scapholunate ligament lesion (partial or complete tear). Results A total of 889 patients were included. Complete paired data were available for 864 patients with a mean age of 42.4 ± 15.4 years (range 10-83 years). 51.3% were male. MRI classified the ligament as intact in 83.9%, partially ruptured in 9.1%, and completely ruptured in 6.9%. Arthroscopy identified intact ligaments in 78.2%, partial tears in 12.9%, and complete tears in 8.9%. In this cohort, MRI demonstrated high specificity (91.1%, 95% CI 89.0-93.3) but limited sensitivity (42.0%, 95% CI 35.0-49.1) for scapholunate ligament lesions. Conclusion In standard clinical practice, preoperative wrist MRI shows high specificity but insufficient sensitivity for detecting scapholunate ligament injuries. In this cohort, MRI detected intact ligaments reliably, but a relevant proportion of partial and complete tears remained unrecognized.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution.
abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut.

title: CT-based deep learning for identifying sinonasal inverted papilloma: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: This study aimed to develop a CT-based deep learning model as a decision-support system for the classification of sinonasal inverted papilloma (IP), nasal polyps, and normal paranasal anatomy. A retrospective dataset of 871 patients who underwent paranasal CT imaging between 2020 and 2024 was analyzed. All diagnoses were confirmed histopathologically. Two representative CT slices per patient were selected at the patient level by an experienced radiologist blinded to final diagnosis. The dataset was split into 70% training and 30% testing sets, with 20% of the training data used for validation. No clinical variables were included; the model relied solely on imaging data. A ResNet50-based convolutional neural network and a Vision Transformer model were trained and compared. The ResNet50 model achieved a test accuracy of 98.47%, outperforming the Vision Transformer model (79.65%). The model demonstrated high class-wise performance, particularly for inverted papilloma detection. A CT-based deep learning model can serve as a decision-support tool for the classification of sinonasal inverted papilloma. Rather than replacing histopathology, this approach may assist clinical triage and complement conventional diagnostic workflows in a hybrid diagnostic strategy.

title: Improved assessment of the cochlear implant and temporal bone structures with ultra-high resolution photon-counting detector CT compared to conventional CT systems.
abstract: Purpose This study evaluates the image quality of photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) compared to conventional CT systems in cochlear implant imaging and aims to determine optimal scan parameters. Methods Three cochlear implant models were inserted into three post-mortem human specimen heads. Each head was scanned on three high-end CT systems: SOMATOM Edge, SOMATOM Force and NAEOTOM Alpha. A total of 192 reconstructions were obtained, including various tube voltages (120-150 kV), tin filtering, and slice thicknesses (0.2-0.6 mm). For each scanner, multiple reconstruction kernels were applied. Contrast-to-noise ratios (CNR) for bone-to-soft-tissue were calculated. Two radiologists independently assessed anatomy, implant visibility, and overall image quality on a 5-point Likert scale and scored diagnostic confidence for detecting anatomic dehiscence. Results PCD-CT showed significantly higher image quality scores across implant, anatomy, and general image quality compared to the Edge and Force (p < 0.001). PCD-CT also produced significantly higher CNR (mean 23.5 vs. 13.8 [Edge] and 12.7 [Force]) and greater diagnostic confidence. For PCD-CT, optimal image quality was achieved using 0.2 mm slice thickness and the Hr89 kernel at 140 kV. PCD-CT scans acquired with half dose (27.5 mGy) showed no significant difference in CNRs but led to slightly lower subjective scores compared to standard-dose imaging. Conclusion PCD-CT provides superior image quality and diagnostic confidence in cochlear implant imaging compared to the Edge and Force. Optimal results are achieved using 140 kV, 0.2 mm slices, and the Hr89 kernel. Although dose reduction is feasible, it slightly compromises subjective image quality.

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of cerebrospinal fluid leak in skull base surgery: a scoping review.
abstract: Background Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak remains one of the most significant complications of skull base surgery, particularly in endoscopic endonasal and transsphenoidal approaches. Accurate risk stratification may improve surgical planning and reconstruction strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have been increasingly investigated for CSF leak prediction; however, the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to map the current literature and summarize data sources, modeling approaches, validation strategies, and reported performance. Methods This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligibility was structured using the Population-Concept-Context framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from 2019 to 2025. Two authors independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts and independently charted data using a standardized table; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Eligible original human studies applied AI/ML to predict perioperative surgical CSF leak or to derive an imaging biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak/encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. No formal protocol was prepared or registered. Results Fifty-five records were identified, and nine primary studies met the eligibility criteria after duplicate removal and full-text assessment. Six studies predicted intraoperative CSF leak, two predicted postoperative leak, and one evaluated a deep-learning-derived CT biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak or encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. Three studies used classical machine-learning methods, four used predominantly deep neural-network or convolutional-neural-network approaches, one compared classical models with a feedforward neural network, and one used a BERT-based natural-language-processing model. One study reported prospective temporal validation; none reported independent external validation at another institution. Among studies reporting AUC, values ranged from 0.69 to 1.00; accuracy, where reported, ranged from 70% to 98.33%. Conclusions AI-based prediction of CSF leak is a promising but evolving field. Methodological heterogeneity and the absence of independent external validation constrain clinical translation. Future studies should prioritize standardized outcomes, multicenter datasets, and prospective validation to support integration into clinical decision-making.

title: Updated dosimetric comparison of HDR interventional radiotherapy including 60 Co sources versus VMAT and electron beam therapy for NMSC.
abstract: Non-melanoma skin cancers (NMSCs), primarily basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma, are the most common malignancies worldwide and frequently arise on the scalp, where complex curvature and anatomical constraints make treatment planning challenging. While surgery remains the standard approach, radiotherapy, particularly high-dose-rate interventional radiotherapy (HDR-IRT, modern brachytherapy), has become an important alternative for patients who are not ideal surgical candidates. Previous dosimetric analyses have demonstrated that 192 I HDR-IRT provides superior target coverage and dose conformity compared with external beam techniques such as volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) and electron beam therapy (EBT). However, the reproducibility of these findings across centres and radioactive sources, including 60 Co, has not been systematically validated. This study aimed to independently validate prior dosimetric results by independently replanning the same cohort of 25 patients with scalp NMSC using 60 Co HDR-IRT. The objective was to assess whether the dosimetric advantages of HDR-IRT remain consistent when different operators, institutions, and isotopes are employed, and to compare 60 Co HDR-IRT with VMAT and EBT under identical clinical conditions. A retrospective dosimetric comparison was conducted using the original CT datasets from 25 patients previously analyzed with 192 Ir HDR-IRT. At an independent institution, new plans were generated for 60 Co HDR-IRT, VMAT, and EBT using the same contours, applicator geometry, prescription doses, and V 95% constraints. HDR-IRT plans were constructed in Oncentra Brachy v4.6 based on TG-43 formalism; VMAT and EBT plans were generated in Eclipse TPS v16.1 using 6 MV photons and 6 MeV electrons, respectively. Dosimetric parameters (V 90% , V 95% , V 100% , D 90% , D mean , D max ) and brain D2cc values were extracted from DVHs. Statistical comparisons were performed with the Mann-Whitney U test (p < 0.05). All techniques provided comparable V 90% (> 99%) and V 95% values, ensuring consistent baseline coverage. However, HDR-IRT using Co-60 demonstrated significantly higher V 100% , D 90% , and D mean values than VMAT and EBT across all prescription groups (p < 0.05). This reflects the proximity of the source to the target and the steep dose gradient inherent to brachytherapy. VMAT produced the most homogeneous dose distributions but at the expense of slightly reduced high-dose coverage. EBT performed adequately for small, flat lesions but showed pronounced limitations in large or curved anatomies, with increased variability and occasional hotspots in the brain. Brain D 2cc doses remained comparable across modalities (p > 0.05), confirming adequate protection of critical structures. This external validation confirms that HDR-IRT retains its dosimetric superiority over VMAT and EBT even when replanned by different operators, at a different institution, and using an alternative isotope ( 60 Co instead of 192 Ir). The findings demonstrate that HDR-IRT is a robust and reproduciblemodality for scalp NMSC, capable of achieving excellent target coverage and rapid dose fall-off without compromising organ-at-risk sparing. These results strengthen the evidence supporting HDR-IRT as a reliable option for treating superficial scalp cancers across diverse clinical settings.

title: Prediction of short-term and long-term responses to cladribine in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: a Danish nationwide real-world study.
abstract: Cladribine is regarded highly efficacious in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). However, prediction of treatment response and optimal management remain elusive, particularly during long-term. We screened the Danish Multiple Sclerosis Registry for patients with RRMS who received ≥2 5-day treatment cycles of cladribine and were followed for >90 days. Annualised relapse rates (ARR) and activity parameters (relapses or MRI activity) were analysed from 90 days after the first dose (index) to year 3 (short-term) together with time-to-first 24-week confirmed disability worsening (CDW), CDW independent of relapses (PIRA), and activity/CDW (loss of "no evidence of disease activity", NEDA-3). Kaplan-Meier log-rank tests were validated in a subgroup who completed ≥4 five-day cladribine cycles before year 3 and contributed with >3 years follow-up (3YFS). Predicting covariables included age (< /≥ 45 years), pre-baseline activity, and short-term NEDA-3 status regarding 3YFS outcomes beyond year 3 (long-term). ARR declined significantly from ~0.55 in the year pre-baseline to ~0.23-0.25 from index to year 3. Younger age and pre-baseline activity predicted more frequent short-term activity. Pre-baseline activity additionally predicted short-term NEDA-3 loss. Short-term findings were consistent in 3YFS patients. CDW and PIRA were rare during short-term (~ 10%) and long-term (~ 20%), even in older patients. However, during long-term, NEDA-3 loss resumed steadily and this was largely unpredictable. While cladribine showed sustained short-term efficacy, treatment response appeared more favourable in older patients and patients without pre-baseline activity. Rare CDW and PIRA events warrant more research in cladribine for disability prevention. Optimal long-term management following cladribine treatment requires more research.

title: Neuroimaging signatures of facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy (FOSMN).
abstract: Facial onset sensory and motor neuronopathy (FOSMN) is an exceptionally rare condition characterized by progressive facial paresthesia and the subsequent appearance of bulbar symptoms with rostro-caudal motor and sensory deficits sometimes extending to the hand muscles. The pathophysiological understanding of this disorder is very limited. In order to identify patterns of neuroanatomical involvement within the brain, we applied advanced magnetic resonance imaging-based techniques to a group of six patients with the diagnosis of FOSMN, using unbiased analysis techniques with atlas-based volumetry of volume-rendering T1-weighted data and whole brain-based spatial statistics of diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). The volumetric data showed significant global atrophy with prominent involvement of the medulla oblongata, while DTI demonstrated significant decreases in the right-hemispheric frontal lobe and bilaterally along the superior and inferior longitudinal fasciculi. In summary, this application of volumetry and DTI to a group of FOSMN patients demonstrated, beyond global brain atrophy as a correlate of a systemic disease process, regional atrophy in the brainstem/medulla oblongata, together with tract alterations of polymodal frontotemporoparietal interconnections. Future neuroimaging studies in larger patient groups of FOSMN are needed for detailed phenotype-neuroimaging correlations.

title: Retinal layer thickness as a potential marker for future cardiovascular events - a UK Biobank cohort study using optical coherence tomography.
abstract: Aims Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. For CVD prevention, effective screening is needed to identify high-risk individuals. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides a noninvasive, low-cost "quick look" into the brain and has recently shown thinning of certain retinal layers in patients with previous CVD. We explored if OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses could predict future major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: stroke/myocardial infarction/cardiovascular death). Methods In this retrospective cohort study, data of 51,293 participants from the UK Biobank were analyzed. We used cause-specific hazard models to evaluate the association of retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness with incident MACE, adjusting models for cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and performed subanalyses for association with incident stroke and myocardial infarction. Results Median follow-up time was 14.7 years. Both RNFL thickness (aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, p < 0.001) and GCIPL thickness (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.92-1.00, p = 0.04) were statistically associated with incident MACE in cause-specific hazard models adjusted for CVRF. Interestingly, RNFL thickness was more strongly associated with incident myocardial infarction (aHR 0.94, 95% CI 0.88-0.99, p = 0.02) while GCIPL was more strongly associated with incident stroke (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, p = 0.003). Conclusion RNFL and GCIPL thicknesses are associated with future MACE, even after adjusting for CVRF. OCT-measured retinal layer thickness could contribute to the assessment of cardiovascular risk.

title: En face visualization of the outer choroidal vessels in regions with geographic atrophy.
abstract: Background To investigate the relationship between choroidal vessel visibility on en face OCT and the preservation status of outer retinal structures within areas of complete RPE and outer retinal atrophy (cRORA) in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Methods In this retrospective observational study, we analyzed 54 eyes from 54 patients with GA due to AMD. All eyes underwent swept-source OCT imaging with 6 × 6 mm volumetric scans centered on the fovea. En face OCT structural images were created using a slab positioned from 64 to 400 μm under Bruch's membrane. Choroidal vessels were classified as highly visible or scarcely visible, while ellipsoid zone (EZ) and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) were categorized as altered or absent. Area and perimeter of atrophic lesions were measured, and locations were classified as foveal, parafoveal, or perifoveal. Results Among the 54 cRORA lesions, 38 eyes (70.4%) exhibited highly visible choroidal vessels, while 16 eyes (29.6%) showed scarcely visible vessels. In areas with highly visible vessels, the EZ was altered in 81.6% of cases, compared to only 12.5% in areas with scarcely visible vessels (p\<0.001). Similarly, lesions with visible vessels were larger and showed a lower proportion of absent RPE (10.5%) than lesions with scarcely visible vessels (62.5%). Interestingly, lesions with highly visible vessels were significantly larger (mean area: 3.30 ± 3.90 mm²) than those with scarcely visible vessels (1.45 ± 2.02 mm², p = 0.024). Conclusions Our study reveals an unexpected association between high choroidal vessel visibility on en face OCT and altered rather than absent outer retinal structures in cRORA. This suggests greater heterogeneity within atrophic lesions than previously recognized and challenges conventional understanding of structure-visibility relationships in atrophic AMD.

title: Genetic characterization of inherited retinal dystrophy in a Northwestern Chinese cohort: A single-center study over a 5-year period in Shaanxi, China.
abstract: Objective Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a clinically and molecularly heterogeneous group of monogenic disorders that cause vision loss across all age groups. This study set out to define the mutational landscape of IRDs among patients evaluated at a tertiary center in Northwest China. Methods Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed in 116 patients with IRDs enrolled at our ophthalmic center over a five-year recruitment period. Of these, 92 underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES) and the remaining 24 were analyzed with a targeted hereditary eye disease enrichment panel (HEDEP). Co-segregation analysis involving family members was completed for 111 probands. Results In total, 129 sequence alterations were detected, of which 60 were novel. The potential molecular diagnostic rate was 69%. High detection rates were observed in clinically well-defined conditions: Stargardt disease, congenital stationary night blindness, fundus albipunctatus, and Bardet-Biedl syndrome each reached 100% diagnostic confirmation. Diagnostic success was greater among patients with available family co-segregation data (70.2%), children and adolescents (76.7%), and those enrolled within the most recent two years (76.2%). Among the 80 molecularly solved/possibly solved cases, autosomal dominant transmission accounted for 17.5%, autosomal recessive inheritance predominated at 65%, and X-linked inheritance accounted for 17.5%. ABCA4 was the most frequently mutated gene in this cohort, followed by BEST1 and CRB1. Notably, no EYS variants were identified, whereas variants in the RDH gene were seen at a relatively higher frequency. Conclusion The present work provides a comprehensive molecular characterization of IRD patients from Northwest China evaluated at a tertiary center in Shaanxi and describes the genetic characteristics of this regional cohort. These observations may help refine diagnostic algorithms for retinal disorders and inform the development of broadly applicable precision treatments.

title: Optical coherence tomography angiography of the macular retina and choroid in glaucoma: a narrative review.
abstract: Glaucoma is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by retinal ganglion cell degeneration, structural remodeling of the retina and choroid, and irreversible visual field loss. Increasing evidence indicates that microvascular dysfunction plays a crucial role in its onset and progression. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), as a noninvasive, high-resolution imaging technique, enables quantitative visualization of retinal and choroidal microcirculation, providing new insights into the structural-vascular-functional relationships in glaucoma. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in the use of OCTA for evaluating macular retinal and choroidal changes in glaucoma, emphasizing its potential in early diagnosis, disease monitoring, and postoperative assessment. Moreover, retinal OCTA vessel-density parameters are closely associated with visual field impairment, whereas the prognostic value of many choroidal metrics remains less well established. With continuous technological innovation and deeper understanding of ocular hemodynamics, OCTA is expected to play an increasingly important role in the early detection and comprehensive management of glaucoma.

title: Combined use of orbital soft tissue volume and retinal microvessel density for diagnosing dysthyroid optic neuropathy.
abstract: Purpose To (i) detect changes in orbital soft tissue and retinal microstructure occurring in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), (ii) investigate the relationship between these variables and their bearing on visual impairment, and (iii) determine their combined diagnostic utility for dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON). Methods Enrolled in this retrospective study were patients with TAO eyes, which included the DON group, equivocal DON (eDON) and non-DON (nDON). Patients were divided into three experimental groups: DON (n = 18 eyes), eDON (n = 24 eyes), and nDON (n = 20 eyes). At the same time, a healthy control (C) group was included (n = 30 eyes). A three-dimensional (3D) volume index, obtained by reconstructing orbital soft tissue via computed tomography (CT) and Mimics software, was used. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) was used to monitor and record retinal microstructural properties, i.e., microvessel density and thickness. Results The DON group had significantly lower density and thickness of the retinal vasculature compared to the other groups (p < 0.05), with the exception of deep macular capillary density (MDRCP-VD), which was not statistically significant. In terms of soft-tissue volumes, the DON group had considerably higher orbital fat (OFV/BOV) and extraocular muscle indices (EOMV/BOV) than did the other groups; in contrast, the muscle cone inner volume index (MCIV/BOV) was lower (p < 0.05). A combination of the macular superficial retinal capillary plexuses (MSCRP-VD), optic nerve head vessel density-whole images (ONH-wiVD), MCIV/BOV, and EOMV/BOV yielded the highest values (AUC: 0.954, sensitivity: 95%, specificity: 88.1%) for the diagnosis of DON compared to the other groups. Conclusions EOMV/BOV plus MCIV/BOV, combined with MSRPC-VD plus ONH-wiVD, appears to provide the most accurate diagnostic guideline for DON. Further, 3D reconstructions of orbital soft tissue, in conjunction with OCT-A images, offer an innovative approach not only for preventing permanent loss of vision but also for enhancing the accuracy of diagnosing DON and its early stages.

title: Integrated multimodal assessment of retinal oxygenation, hemodynamics, and neurovisual function in retinal vein occlusion.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to characterize retinal hemodynamics, oxygenation and oxygen kinetics, and neurovisual alterations in retinal vein occlusion (RVO) using an integrated ocular multimodal imaging system. Methods This cross-sectional study included 105 eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO), central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), or no retinal disease. RVO eyes were either untreated or previously treated with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor. The system simultaneously assessed retinal oxygenation and oxygen kinetics, vascular structure, blood flow and pulsatility, pupillary light reflex (PLR), and smooth pursuit eye movements (SPEM). Results The study included untreated CRVO (n = 12), previously treated CRVO (n = 23), untreated BRVO (n = 14), previously treated BRVO (n = 32), and healthy controls (n = 24). At the nominal P < 0.05 level, arterial oxygen saturation was lower in untreated BRVO eyes than in healthy controls (raw P = 0.0315) and higher in previously treated than in untreated BRVO eyes (raw P = 0.0456). Venous oxygen saturation was lower in untreated CRVO and both BRVO groups (raw P = 0.0046-0.0190), and venous oxygen concentration was lower in both BRVO groups (raw P = 0.0060-0.0265). The arteriovenous differences in oxygen saturation and concentration were higher in previously treated CRVO and BRVO eyes (raw P = 0.0090-0.0339), and oxygen extraction fraction was higher in untreated CRVO and previously treated BRVO eyes (raw P = 0.0114-0.0259). Flow acceleration index was higher in both previously treated groups (raw P = 0.0368 and 0.0443). Arterial external diameter (ED a ) was smaller in previously treated CRVO and both BRVO groups (raw P ranging from < 0.0001 to 0.0095). PLR abnormalities were most evident in CRVO, whereas SPEM velocity and velocity gain were higher in all four RVO groups (raw P = 0.0018-0.0175). ED a , PLR, and SPEM differences remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q < 0.05). Exploratory analyses of the relationships between vascular, hemodynamic, oxygenation and oxygen kinetics, and neurovisual measurements identified associations of blood flow velocity, retinal blood flow, and arterial external diameter with PLR and SPEM parameters. Conclusions Integrated multimodal assessment identified distinct patterns of vascular, oxygenation and oxygen-kinetic, and neurovisual abnormalities across RVO groups. PLR abnormalities were mainly observed in CRVO. SPEM abnormalities occurred in both CRVO and BRVO. These findings provide a basis for selecting candidate measurements for future prospective studies of disease progression, treatment-related changes, and visual outcomes using the same platform.

title: Baseline OCT-features predicting retinal atrophy in optic disc swelling.
abstract: To assess optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers at initial presentation of optic disc swelling (ODS) in predicting retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell layer (GCL) atrophy using volumetric macular and optic nerve head (ONH) analysis. In this retrospective study, patients with first-episode ODS and 6- and 12-month follow-up were included. Spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) volumetric scans of the macula and ONH were analysed using an AI-based platform (Discovery). Macular RNFL, ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCL + IPL), and ONH RNFL volumes were quantified across ETDRS grid fields. Longitudinal change was modelled with linear mixed-effects models; predictors of 12-month outcomes were identified by multiple linear regression. Fifty-two eyes from 32 patients (mean age 39 ± 13.8 years) were analysed across papilloedema (n = 24), uveitic disc oedema (n = 22), ischaemic (n = 4), and infiltrative (n = 2) aetiologies. At baseline, uveitic disc oedema eyes showed significantly higher macular RNFL and GCL + IPL volumes than papilloedema, while ONH RNFL was similarly elevated. All OCT parameters declined significantly over 12months, with greater macular loss in uveitic disc oedema cases (p < 0.001). GCL + IPL reduction was more pronounced in the uveitic disc oedema group (- 296 ± 241 nL vs. - 110 ± 160 nL) and persisted beyond 6 months only in this group (p = 0.012). Baseline GCL + IPL volume strongly predicted 12-month GCL + IPL volume loss (β = 0.91, p < 0.001), and worse baseline visual acuity independently predicted more severe GCL + IPL volume loss (β=-317, p = 0.002). ONH RNFL did not predict visual outcomes. ODS is associated with measurable structural change over 12 months. Baseline macular OCT biomarkers, particularly GCL + IPL, predicted 12-month outcomes largely independent of aetiology, and macular OCT may aid risk stratification alongside aetiological diagnosis.

title: Functional detection of external iliac artery endofibrosis in a cyclist: integrating performance metrics and vascular imaging, a case study.
abstract: Purpose Identifying external iliac artery endofibrosis (EIAE) remains challenging and may lead to a reduction in cycling performance. This case study describes diagnosis process and changes in performance prior to and during recovery in a cyclist with EIAE. Power-Duration data, laboratory-based Lactate Thresholds (LT) assessments, and vascular evaluation data were integrated in a comprehensive attempt to characterise performance changes associated with EIAE. Methods The Power-Duration profile was obtained from the 2022-2024 seasons. Graded Exercise Tests were performed 90 days before (GXT1) and 90 and 172 days after treatment (GXT2, GXT3), assessing Power Output (PO) and blood lactate, LT (LTP1, Dmaxmod) were estimated, and left/right leg PO (LPO, RPO). In addition, vascular evaluation under an Exercise-Induced Claudication Test (EICT) was performed. Results Power-Duration profile showed a decline in performance across 5-60-min durations in 2023 and 2024 compared with 2022, with reductions ranging from - 1.2% to - 15.6%. Estimated Left-Right Balance (L/R-B) at LT ranged from 47 to 49% at GXT1, decreased to 46-47% at GXT2, and increased to 52-53% at GXT3, indicating dynamic inter-limb changes throughout time tests. Vascular assessment revealed kinking of the left iliac axis, with suspicion in the right axis, which was confirmed at the end of the study. Conclusion Novel power-based assessments across multiple durations, in this case study, helped to evaluate performance decrements associated with EIAE. Lower-limb PO derived from the GXT appeared sensitive detecting inflection points indicative of performance loss potentially related to underlying vascular pathology. Echo-Doppler provided significant evidence confirmed by intravascular ultrasound and intraoperative findings.

title: Clinical pathways of hospitalized extremity soft-tissue infections: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Bacterial infections of the skin and soft tissues (SSTIs) are common and should be considered a key differential diagnosis in patients presenting with redness and swelling in these areas. They range from mild superficial cases to severe, complicated forms requiring prompt antimicrobial therapy and, often, surgical intervention. We aimed to describe clinical pathways, diagnostic evolution, treatment strategies, and outcomes in a hospitalized orthopedic/trauma surgery cohort. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center analysis of all inpatients treated for extremity SSTIs between January 2020 and December 2023. Extracted variables included demographics, admission and discharge diagnoses, inflammatory markers, imaging, microbiology, surgical procedures, antibiotic regimens and duration, intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, and in-hospital outcomes. Results A total of 242 patients were included (mean age 55.7 ± 20.3 years; 40.1% female), with a median length of stay of 7.5 days. ICU care was required in 25/242 10.3%; in-hospital mortality was 7/242 2.9%. Surgical management was required in 134/242 patients (55.4%). Comorbidity burden was substantial (ASA III-IV: 41.3%), and sepsis was documented in 32/242 (13.2%). Diagnostic classification changed between admission and discharge in 80/242 cases (33.1%) of cases. Inflammatory markers declined markedly from admission to discharge (CRP 43.0 [Range: 0.6-640.2, IQR: 13.2-107.5] to CRP: 13.1 [Range: 0.4-541.0, IQR: 4.6-35.2]; leukocytes 11.9 ± 6.09 10/L to 7.68 ± 4.25 10 9 /L). The hand, lower leg and foot were the most frequent sites. CT was performed in 111/242 (45.9%) and ultrasound in 65/242 (26.9%), with heterogeneous imaging strategies (CT only 87/242 (36.0%), US only 41/242 (16.9%), both 24/242 (9.9%), none 90/242 (37.2%)). CT use clustered with higher admission CRP and higher operative burden, including more re-interventions among operated patients. Cultures were frequently negative; when positive, staphylococci and streptococci predominated. Ampicillin/sulbactam and amoxicillin/clavulanate were the most common antibiotics, with frequent IV combination therapy. Conclusions Hospitalized extremity SSTIs were characterized by frequent diagnostic reclassification, heterogeneous documentation and imaging pathways, and a high rate of operative management despite overall favorable outcomes. CT was more frequently used in patients with higher inflammatory activity and greater procedural burden. originalAbstract:
Background

Bacterial infections of the skin and soft tissues (SSTIs) are common and should be considered a key differential diagnosis in patients presenting with redness and swelling in these areas. They range from mild superficial cases to severe, complicated forms requiring prompt antimicrobial therapy and, often, surgical intervention. We aimed to describe clinical pathways, diagnostic evolution, treatment strategies, and outcomes in a hospitalized orthopedic/trauma surgery cohort.

Methods

We performed a retrospective single-center analysis of all inpatients treated for extremity SSTIs between January 2020 and December 2023. Extracted variables included demographics, admission and discharge diagnoses, inflammatory markers, imaging, microbiology, surgical procedures, antibiotic regimens and duration, intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, and in-hospital outcomes.

Results

A total of 242 patients were included (mean age 55.7 ± 20.3 years; 40.1% female), with a median length of stay of 7.5 days. ICU care was required in 25/242 10.3%; in-hospital mortality was 7/242 2.9%. Surgical management was required in 134/242 patients (55.4%). Comorbidity burden was substantial (ASA III-IV: 41.3%), and sepsis was documented in 32/242 (13.2%). Diagnostic classification changed between admission and discharge in 80/242 cases (33.1%) of cases. Inflammatory markers declined markedly from admission to discharge (CRP 43.0 [Range: 0.6-640.2, IQR: 13.2-107.5] to CRP: 13.1 [Range: 0.4-541.0, IQR: 4.6-35.2]; leukocytes 11.9 ± 6.09 10/L to 7.68 ± 4.25 109/L). The hand, lower leg and foot were the most frequent sites. CT was performed in 111/242 (45.9%) and ultrasound in 65/242 (26.9%), with heterogeneous imaging strategies (CT only 87/242 (36.0%), US only 41/242 (16.9%), both 24/242 (9.9%), none 90/242 (37.2%)). CT use clustered with higher admission CRP and higher operative burden, including more re-interventions among operated patients. Cultures were frequently negative; when positive, staphylococci and streptococci predominated. Ampicillin/sulbactam and amoxicillin/clavulanate were the most common antibiotics, with frequent IV combination therapy.

Conclusions

Hospitalized extremity SSTIs were characterized by frequent diagnostic reclassification, heterogeneous documentation and imaging pathways, and a high rate of operative management despite overall favorable outcomes. CT was more frequently used in patients with higher inflammatory activity and greater procedural burden. This descriptive association may, at least in part, reflect differences in clinical severity and selection for imaging. The findings support structured reassessment and targeted imaging when anatomical clarification is likely to alter management.

title: Primary and secondary vasculitis of the lung - critical evaluation of the update classification.
abstract: Vasculitis in the lung can be separated into infectious and non-infectious, and in systemic and localized ones. Three major categories in the lung are known, previously named Wegener's granulomatosis, Churg-Strauss syndrome, and microscopic polyangiitis. The classification of vasculitis was proposed in 1994, including a size distribution for each type, an antinuclear and anticytoplasmic antibody profile (ANCA), and an organ location. In an updated classification (2011) the names for two of the most common primary vasculitis were replaced: Wegener`s granulomatosis by Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) and Churg-Strauss syndrome by Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA). This proposal has been critically discussed in meetings of the pulmonary working group of ESP (2025) and the Pulmonary Pathology Society Meeting (Quebec, 2026). There were doubts about the usefulness of the when applied in pulmonary pathology. A new proposal is presented here. This classification is based on pattern recognition, such as neutrophilic, eosinophilic, and other forms of vasculitis. As many other types of pulmonary vasculitis were not covered in the old nor in the new proposal, several variants are added. This applies for example to vasculitis seen in autoimmune diseases. There is no doubt, that a classification of vasculitis is important, to sort the type of vasculitis. If possible, such a classification should be useful not only in lung pathology but more general in any other organ system. However, in several organ systems the clinical picture and the laboratory test allow a diagnosis, which is not the case in lung. On CT scan most types of pulmonary vasculitis present with ground glass opacitis with/without nodules. Often biopsies are labelled as interstitial lung disease.

title: Receptor architecture shapes the regional organization of the macaque cingulate cortex.
abstract: The cingulate cortex plays a central role in emotion, motivation, decision-making and motor control, yet its internal organization in the macaque brain remains debated. In the present study, we examined the cyto- and receptor architectonic organization of the macaque cingulate cortex and provide a 3D parcellation of the identified areas in both surface and volumetric representations. Multivariate receptor analyses consistently separated areas of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and anterior midcingulate cortex (aMCC) from those of the posterior midcingulate cortex (pMCC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), supporting the definition of four principal cingulate regions in the macaque brain. These regions are characterized by distinct receptor balances: the ACC is enriched with glutamatergic and monoaminergic receptors; the aMCC exhibits high densities of modulatory receptors; the pMCC is characterized by overall lowest receptor densities; and the PCC displays intermediate receptor densities with relatively higher GABA A and M 3 receptors. Within the ACC, receptor architecture revealed differentiation of subgenual, gyral and sulcal portions, while the PCC contained subdivisions corresponding to dorsal and ventral PCC. Cytoarchitectonic and receptor analyses further demonstrated that cortex along the dorsal bank of the cingulate sulcus (cgs) contains distinct cingulate areas extending from the sulcal fundus onto the dorsal wall, indicating that it forms part of the cingulate cortex rather than the frontal cortex or a transitional zone between those regions. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive anatomical and neurochemical framework for the macaque cingulate cortex and address the long-standing controversy regarding the dorsal bank of the cgs.

title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups. However, targeted region-of-interest ROI analyses demonstrated lower right amygdala and bilateral hippocampal volumes in patients with MCI. Cortical thickness analyses identified two regions with lower thickness in MCI: the right superior parietal lobule and the left posterior insula. A significant Group × Sadness interaction indicated that the association between left superior parietal gray matter volume and sadness recognition differed between groups. Follow-up analyses of the extracted values showed a positive association in MCI, although this within-group association did not reach statistical significance, and a significant inverse association in HCs. These findings suggest that early MCI involves selective thinning in association cortices supporting attention and salience processing. The sadness-specific interaction indicates that patients with MCI may rely on preserved superior parietal structure during sadness recognition, a pattern that is consistent with structural reserve accounts, although this interpretation remains speculative given the cross-sectional design.

title: Mediastinal lymphadenitis caused by Mycobacterium avium complex in children: a rare case of airway compression.
abstract: Airway compression caused by intrathoracic non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) lymphadenitis is particularly uncommon in otherwise healthy children and remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the clinical, radiological, microbiological, and immunological features of a French pediatric cohort diagnosed with mediastinal Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lymphadenitis. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study that included children diagnosed with bacteriologically confirmed intrathoracic MAC lymphadenitis in France between 2009 and 2024. Patients with HIV-related immunodeficiency or known inborn errors of immunity were excluded. Immunological investigations were performed, including the secretion of IL-12 and IFN-γ by a whole-blood assay. Ten children with intrathoracic MAC lymphadenitis with airway compression were included. In most cases, the diagnosis required invasive sampling. Mycobacterium avium was identified in nine patients and M. intracellulare in one patient. Main respiratory manifestations were dyspnea, persistent cough, and abnormal breath sounds. Chest computed tomography (CT) scans revealed mediastinal lymphadenopathies causing airway compression, ventilation disorders, and air trapping. Following prolonged antibiotic treatment, all patients showed clinical improvement and a reduction in lymph node size, although residual calcifications frequently persisted. IFN-γ secretion was impaired in all five patients who underwent specific immunological testing, consistently lower compared with healthy controls. Conclusion This study highlights a rare presentation of airway compression in children characterized by MAC mediastinal lymphadenitis. These findings underscore the importance of considering NTM infections in the differential diagnosis of persistent mediastinal lymphadenitis in young children and highlight the frequent need for invasive sampling to establish a microbiological diagnosis. Although no overt immunodeficiency was identified, immune evaluation, particularly exploration of the IFN-γ-mediated immunity, may be relevant in these patients. What is known • Mediastinal lymphadenitis caused by non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) is a rare condition, mainly reported in immunocompromised patients, and often mimics tuberculosis on imaging. • Diagnosis is challenging due to nonspecific clinical and radiological findings, and it relies on microbiological confirmation. What is new • In this cohort, intrathoracic MAC infection in young children presented as airway-compressive mediastinal lymphadenitis rather than classical parenchymal pulmonary NTM disease. • Bronchoalveolar lavage had a low diagnostic yield, and most cases required targeted lymph node or endobronchial granuloma sampling. • A subset of tested patients showed reduced IFN-γ secretion despite the absence of a known monogenic immunodeficiency.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of hybrid versus conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection for non-ampullary duodenal submucosal tumors.
abstract: Background and aims Hybrid endoscopic submucosal dissection (H-ESD) is established to be curable and safe for colorectal submucosal tumors (SMTs). We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of H-ESD and conventional ESD (C-ESD) for non-ampullary duodenal SMTs (NAD-SMTs). Methods From September 2017 to December 2024, patients with NAD-SMTs treated with H-ESD or C-ESD at the Endoscopy Center of Zhongshan Hospital were retrospectively analyzed. After propensity score matching (PSM), baseline characteristics, clinical outcomes, and follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. Results With similar baseline characteristics between the two groups after PSM, the H-ESD group had a shorter procedural duration (41 vs. 67 min, P < 0.001) compared to the C-ESD group. The en bloc resection rates were 93.8 and 92.2%, and the R0 resection rates were 90.6 and 89.1%, respectively. Although there was no statistically significant difference, the H-ESD group had a lower overall adverse event (AE) rate. The H-ESD group had 1 case of abdominal effusion and 1 case of febrile episode, whereas the C-ESD group had 2 cases of intraprocedural bleeding, 1 case of intraoperative muscle layer injury, 1 case of pneumoperitoneum, 1 case of delayed bleeding, and 1 case of abdominal effusion. During the median follow-up period, no recurrence occurred in the H-ESD group, while one local recurrence was detected in the C-ESD group. Conclusions Both H-ESD and C-ESD were safe and effective for NAD-SMTs; however, H-ESD resulted in a reduced procedure time without increasing the occurrence of AEs compared with C-ESD. Therefore, H-ESD may be recommended as a treatment for NAD-SMTs.

title: Impact of puncture site location in percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage on outcomes of subsequent laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a multicenter retrospective clinical study.
abstract: Background Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGD) followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is an effective treatment strategy for acute cholecystitis (AC). However, the impact of the PTGD puncture site on subsequent LC outcomes has not been systematically investigated. Methods This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with AC who underwent PTGD followed by LC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University (January 2018-May 2025) and Yingkou Central Hospital (January 2020-May 2025). PTGD was performed according to the Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18) and individualized clinical judgment. Based on CT imaging, patients were categorized into two groups according to the PTGD puncture site: the fundus group (n = 208), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder fundus, and the neck group (n = 47), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder neck. Clinical parameters compared included baseline characteristics, gallbladder neck stone impaction, post-PTGD hospital stay, LC operative time, difficult gallbladder, intraoperative injuries and hemorrhage, post-LC complications, drainage placement and duration after LC, total hospital stay for LC, post-LC hospital stay, and hospitalization expenses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the independent association between puncture site and perioperative outcomes. Results In univariate analyses, no significant differences were observed between the fundus and neck groups regarding intraoperative injuries or major postoperative complications. Compared with the neck group, the fundus group demonstrated significantly shorter LC operative time, a lower incidence of difficult gallbladder, fewer drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, reduced post-LC hospital stay, and lower hospitalization expenses (P < 0.05). In multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses, after adjusting for sex, age, body mass index (BMI), gallbladder neck stone impaction, interval between PTGD and LC, and TG18 severity grade, fundus-adjacent puncture remained independently associated with a lower risk of difficult gallbladder, reduced drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, shorter post-LC and total hospital stays, and lower hospitalization expenses. In addition, fundus-adjacent puncture was associated with a 11.93 min reduction in LC operative time, although the association did not reach statistical significance (95%CI - 24.40 to 0.54; P = 0.061). Conclusions PTGD with puncture site adjacent to the gallbladder fundus is associated with improved surgical efficiency and reduced postoperative burden during subsequent LC. These findings suggest that fundus-adjacent puncture may be a favorable approach in clinical practice for optimizing patient outcomes following PTGD when technically feasible and clinically appropriate.

title: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy obstruction after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a systematic review.
abstract: Hemobezoar-related jejunojejunostomy (JJ) obstruction is a rare early complication after minimally invasive Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB). Although early small bowel obstruction after RYGB is well described, obstruction caused by hemobezoar formation remains poorly characterized. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261320591). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 2026. Eligible studies reported adults undergoing primary minimally invasive RYGB with early hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction. Data were extracted on study characteristics, presentation, diagnostic modality, operative strategy, gastric decompression, and outcomes. Given its rarity and lack of comparative cohorts, findings were summarized descriptively. Six studies met inclusion criteria, including 7669 minimally invasive RYGB procedures and 29 hemobezoar-related JJ obstructions. The crude incidence was 0.38%, with per-study incidence ranging from 0.09% to 1.94%. Presentation was consistently early, most commonly within 72 postoperative hours, frequently included tachycardia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, hematocrit decline, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Computed tomography with intravenous contrast was the predominant diagnostic modality, demonstrating dilation of the excluded stomach and proximal limbs with hyperdense intraluminal content at the JJ. Operative management evolved from laparotomy with JJ revision in earlier reports to laparoscopic clot evacuation with selective revision when anastomotic compromise, leak, ischemia, or ongoing bleeding was identified. Gastric remnant decompression was emphasized to reduce closed-loop distension and intraperitoneal contamination. No deaths were reported among 29 cases, although morbidity included abscess formation, anastomotic or staple-line complications, pancreatitis, respiratory complications, readmission, and repeat reoperation. Hemobezoar-related JJ obstruction after minimally invasive RYGB is uncommon but important. It typically presents within the first postoperative days with obstructive symptoms and evidence of intraluminal bleeding. Across retrospective studies, favorable outcomes were reported following prompt CT diagnosis, early operative exploration, remnant decompression, and minimally invasive clot evacuation with selective anastomotic revision. Prospective validation of this management approach is needed.

title: Bilateral external oblique intercostal block combined with intravenous patient-controlled analgesia for multimodal analgesia after laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Background Postoperative pain after laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) remains common and peaks within 24 h. Opioid-based analgesia improves pain but can delay recovery, prompting opioid-sparing regional techniques within ERAS pathways. Objective To evaluate whether adding bilateral ultrasound-guided external oblique intercostal plane block (EOIB) to standard intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) improves early analgesia and recovery after elective LC. Methods In a prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled parallel trial, 56 patients were randomized (1:1) to receive bilateral EOIB (n=28) or no regional block (control, n=28). All patients received standardised anesthesia and PCA with butorphanol. The primary outcome was total butorphanol consumption within 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, Quality of Recovery at 24 h, time to first flatus, nausea and vomiting, intraoperative haemodynamic events, and length of hospital stay. Results EOIB significantly reduced 24 h butorphanol consumption [median 3.7 (IQR 3.2-4.8) mg vs. 7.2 (6.2-7.6) mg, equivalent to 18.5 vs. 36.0 mg intravenous morphine]. After adjustment, opioid consumption was 46.5% lower (95% CI 38.3-53.6; P<0.001). EOIB also increased QoR-15 at 24 h (median 140 vs. 131; P<0.001) and shortened time to first flatus (median 18 vs. 20 h; P=0.031). Cough-pain VRS scores were lower with a significant group-by-time interaction (P=0.013). Intraoperative haemodynamics did not differ, and PONV was numerically lower without statistical significance. Conclusion Bilateral EOIB with standard PCA provides clear opioid-sparing effects after LC without increasing safety risks. Study registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07332546.
